qa_audit.doable_note: The two .ai inputs (letters_AZ.ai_authored, numbers_09.ai_authored) fed to document_render_vector in steps 20/21 are neither in inputs[] (only 3 raster images) nor produced by any prior connector step — image_vectorize emits .svg, not .ai, and no connector converts SVG→.ai. So the .ai and .eps deliverables depend on an off-connector authoring/re-wrap step the spec discloses but never realizes with a connector. SVG deliverables (steps 11/19) are fully doable; AI/EPS half is not connector-produced. NOTE: reverify's headline claim that EPS is not a render_vector capability is FALSE — the tool schema explicitly lists application/eps as a supported outputMediaType.
qa_audit.presentation_note: Complete and well-formed: one deliverable (SVG+EPS+AI glyph package), verbatim-grounded full_brief (cand_46, db_i 823), inputs with realism_notes, outputs with specs, coherent parallel-branch workflow, reverify present. Minor weakness: steps 6/14 narrate "referencing collar_ink_ref_licensed" for ink-tone matching, but color_temperature is a global WB adjustment with no target-color sampling, so the licensed collar stock (step 1) does no load-bearing work.
qa_audit.top_issue: The .ai/.eps deliverables (half the required outputs) hinge on an SVG→.ai "authoring" step that is not an enumerated input nor produced by any connector; the SVG core is fully doable and the spec is honest about the gap, so it stays a minor/borderline chain issue rather than a banned-capability failure.
